skill.name: accessibility-engineering
skill.description: Audits existing interfaces for WCAG 2.2 AA conformance and remediates the violations found. Use when auditing a page or component for accessibility, running axe-core or pa11y, triaging a11y violations, or checking screen reader and contrast issues before shipping.
skill.summary: Find and fix web accessibility issues using automated checks and manual testing against WCAG 2.2 AA.
skill.author: addyosmani

security_audit.summary: Most alerts describe Markdown formatting, documentation links, or routine report handling. The script embeds environment-derived paths in JavaScript, automatically runs npm packages, and opens user-supplied targets with no enforced audit scope. Page content enters the reports, but the reviewed files show no evidence of deliberate data exfiltration or embedded prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Temporary report paths are inserted into executable JavaScript.
remediation.suggestion: Keep JavaScript source fixed and pass paths as separate Node arguments, as the report status helper already does.

remediation.issue: The documented workflow and wrapper can download and run npm code without confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Use reviewed local tools with a lockfile for transitive dependencies. Require explicit approval before installing packages or downloading browser components.

remediation.issue: The browser audit does not enforce which destinations or files it can access.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval for the target and validate file paths against the project root. Isolate the browser and restrict network access to approved destinations.

remediation.issue: JSON reports can include page-controlled markup and sensitive content.
remediation.suggestion: Limit raw markup in reports and label retained excerpts as untrusted data. Redact sensitive details before sharing reports or passing them to an assistant.

finding_verdicts.reason: The substitution runs a fixed mktemp command and stores its output as a path. The shell does not execute the returned value.
This calls a fixed report status function with quoted arguments. It assigns the returned status text without interpreting it as a command.
This captures the pa11y report status from a fixed function. The report path and exit code are passed as quoted arguments.
The shebang selects Bash for the documented audit script. It does not use variable input to select or start a command.
The helper receives a script-generated report path as a separate argument and parses the file as JSON. Neither value is evaluated as code.
The result path is inserted into JavaScript passed to Node. An unsafe temporary directory path can change the code instead of supplying a filename.
The axe report path is expanded inside executable JavaScript. A path inherited through TMPDIR can break the intended string literal.
The write uses a path embedded in Node source rather than an argument. Unsafe temporary path characters can alter that source.
The pa11y merge inserts the result path into Node source. That path can be influenced through TMPDIR and is not escaped for JavaScript.
The pa11y report path is expanded into a JavaScript string literal. Parsing the report as JSON does not protect the surrounding source.
The merged report write places the temporary path directly in Node source. Serializing the result as JSON does not escape the path.
The axe fallback size check embeds the temporary path in Node source. Node parses that source even if the fallback never runs.
The pa11y fallback embeds the report path in the generated JavaScript. The path can alter that source before the fallback condition is checked.
This short-lived validator reads a generated report from a separate path argument. Synchronous reading is expected for this CLI check.
The risk is path interpolation, not synchronous reading. The temporary path becomes part of the code that Node executes.
The axe input filename is expanded within the JavaScript program. The shell quoting does not escape it for a JavaScript literal.
The synchronously written report is legitimate. The risk is that the destination path is interpolated into executable source.
The pa11y merge reads its prior result through a path embedded in Node source. The path inherits the generated temporary directory without JavaScript escaping.
The temporary report filename enters executable JavaScript rather than a separate argument. An unsafe path can change the parsed program.
The pa11y merge write repeats the unescaped temporary path interpolation. The synchronous API itself is not the risk.
The text formatter inserts RESULT_FILE into Node source. The value derives from the temporary directory and is not escaped for JavaScript.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Execution of Downloaded Audit Tools
semantic_findings.description: The workflow can download and run npm tools with no installation prompt. Top-level version pins do not replace a reviewed dependency lockfile.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples and wrapper use npx with automatic confirmation. The reviewed bundle contains no lockfile or preapproved local tool setup.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Audit Does Not Enforce Target Scope
semantic_findings.description: The wrapper passes user-supplied URLs and paths to browser tools without enforcing an approved scope. Scans can reach resources available to the runner.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The wrapper checks for missing input and then forwards targets unchanged. The resources reachable in practice depend on the runner and browser configuration.

semantic_findings.title: Page-Controlled Content Enters Audit Reports
semantic_findings.description: Audit reports can include sensitive markup or page text that looks like instructions. Assistants and report recipients should treat those excerpts as untrusted data.

content.user_title: Audit and Fix Web Accessibility Issues
content.value_statement: Automated checks miss barriers that affect users navigating by keyboard or screen reader. Combine scanner findings with manual tests to prioritize fixes and verify them.
actual_capabilities: Run axe-core and pa11y against a web page or pa11y alone against a local HTML file.
Combine automated findings into text or JSON reports with tool versions, status, and severity totals.
Flag incomplete scanner runs instead of reporting a zero-violation total.
Guide manual checks for keyboard navigation, screen reader announcements, contrast, zoom, and reduced motion.
Prioritize verified fixes using native HTML when possible, then repeat the checks to verify the changes.
limitations: Automated results do not prove WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.
The wrapper requires Bash, Node.js, and npm. The toolchain may need network access to fetch packages or browser components.
Local file mode runs only pa11y. Screen reader checks need a browser and assistive technology.
The standalone bundle does not include the referenced checklist or companion resources.

use_cases.title: Fix an inaccessible form
use_cases.description: Verify missing labels and keyboard problems in an existing form. Make targeted fixes and retest the affected controls.

use_cases.title: Verify a release candidate
use_cases.description: Pair scanner reports with manual checks on a staging page. Record the browser, assistive technology, and checks that could not be run.

use_cases.title: Prioritize accessibility findings
use_cases.description: Review verified barriers and separate them from untested items. Use the impact on key user tasks to decide what should be fixed first.

prompt_templates.title: Review a single form
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review an existing component without running a scanner.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this form for missing labels, unclear errors, and keyboard access. Explain each issue and list the manual checks I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Triage a scanner report
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn automated findings into a verification list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these axe-core and pa11y findings. Group reports of the same issue, identify the affected controls, and say how to verify each issue manually.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a checkout fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: test a keyboard and screen reader regression.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a keyboard and screen reader retest for this checkout modal. Check initial focus, Escape, focus return, and error announcements. Mark unavailable checks as untested.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a release candidate
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine scanner evidence and manual checks for a release review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the approved staging page using existing local tools. Ask before installing anything. Compare scanner findings with manual results and separate verified failures from checks that were not run.

output_examples.input: Review a form with an unlabeled email input and an error message shown only in red.
output: The email input needs an associated visible label so assistive technology can announce its purpose.
Add error text and associate it with the input. Verify the error without relying on color.
Screen reader behavior remains untested until someone checks it with a named browser and screen reader.

output_examples.input: Summarize an audit in which axe completed but pa11y did not return a valid report.
output: The URL audit is incomplete. Axe completed, but pa11y did not produce a valid report.
Do not report a combined violation count. Resolve the pa11y failure and rerun the audit.

best_practices: Verify each automated finding in the browser before changing the interface.
Use native HTML controls where possible and retest behavior after each fix.
Record the browser, assistive technology, and checks that were not run.
anti_patterns: Claiming conformance after a clean automated scan.
Adding ARIA labels to custom controls without fixing their keyboard behavior.
Running an audit on an unapproved target or sharing raw reports without checking for sensitive content.

faq.question: Can this skill certify WCAG 2.2 AA conformance?
faq.answer: No. It helps find and fix barriers, but conformance requires evaluating all applicable criteria, including checks that automated tools cannot perform.

faq.question: Which tools run in URL and file modes?
faq.answer: URL mode runs axe-core and pa11y. Local HTML file mode runs only pa11y.

faq.question: What do I need to run the wrapper?
faq.answer: You need Bash, Node.js, and npm. The wrapper can fetch and run the pinned packages when they are not already available.

faq.question: What happens when a scanner fails?
faq.answer: The wrapper reports an incomplete run and does not produce a combined violation total.

faq.question: Will the skill verify screen reader behavior for me?
faq.answer: It provides a testing workflow. A check stays untested until someone verifies it with a named browser and screen reader.

faq.question: Can a report contain sensitive page content?
faq.answer: Yes. JSON reports can contain HTML and text extracted from audited pages. Review and redact them before sharing.
